sentences.text: Estimates for Tarascosaurus vary significantly; some sources suggest a length of 7 to 9 meters, while the primary description based on the holotype indicates a smaller size of 2.5 to 3 meters.
The genus name honors the Tarasque, a devouring monster from folklore, while the specific name salluvicus refers to the Gallic tribe that lived near ancient Marseille.
Buffetaut and Le Loeuff named and described Tarascosaurus salluvicus in 1991 after finding the holotype specimen PSL 330201 in the Fuvelian Beds.
Additional material referred to the genus includes a paratype of two dorsal vertebrae and a damaged tail vertebra.
Tarascosaurus lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 to 71 million years ago, in what is now Europe.

Originally placed in the Abelisauridae in 1991, the classification became controversial when Allain and Pereda-Suberbiola argued in 2003 that the type specimen lacked uniquely abelisaurid traits and should be considered a nomen dubium.
Oliver Rauhut also concluded in 2003 that the available material was not diagnostic enough to support the species' validity.
However, phylogenetic analyses conducted in the 2020s have supported the original classification of Tarascosaurus as an abelisaurid.
